As of 355 AM Thursday... 

KEY MESSAGE 1... An increasingly active pattern will support a 
couple of episodes of coastal cyclogenesis along the South and 
Middle Atlantic coasts, and associated chances of rain in cntl NC, 
late this weekend and again mid next week. 

The models continue to indicate a lead shortwave perturbation, in an 
increasingly-energetic srn stream jet extending across the 
subtropical ern N. Pacific and evident this morning in GOES 
satellite data over MX, will amplify and assume negative while 
pivoting across the GOM and FL through Sat. Another will follow and 
possibly phase with the lead perturbation as it pivots across the 
South Atlantic states through the remainder of the weekend, during 
which time a nrn stream shortwave perturbation will progress across 
the nrn N. Pacific and into CA. Although model spread increases with 
time through next week, the consensus of guidance depicts 
considerable amplification of that shortwave feature as it 
progresses into the OH Valley and Middle Atlantic by Thanksgiving.

At the surface, low pressure is forecast to develop invof The 
Bahamas by Fri, as forcing for ascent related to the lead 
subtropical perturbation overspreads and interacts with an east/west-
oriented, quasi-stationary baroclinic zone that has become 
suppressed across far srn FL and The Bahamas, along the srn 
periphery of an expansive and persistent Canadian high and cP 
airmass across the ern US. That frontal low should be both 
baroclinic/attached to the frontal zone and in an environment 
characterized by around 20-30 kts of 250-300 mb flow and shear. 
Except for directly within the upr-level trough axis, similar shear 
will likely persist off the South Atlantic coast through the 
weekend, as the subtropical jet noses across the region. Despite 
what some models and most notably the GFS have indicated due to 
convective feedback in recent days, substantial deepening of the 
low, at least initially, will be unlikely given a relative lack of 
forcing accompanying the subtropical perturbation. As thermal 
advection strengthens surrounding the developing low, "self-
development" may contribute to more substantial deepening of the low 
as it tracks along and just offshore the South Atlantic coast, while 
probably remaining attached to the frontal zone separating modified 
continental air over the ern US and a maritime Tropical airmass 
advected/retreating poleward across the wrn Atlantic/ahead of the 
low. Tropical development consequently appears much less likely than 
extratropical or perhaps sub-tropical deepening/development. Despite 
better agreement/less spread in the track of the low in AI and 
dynamical ensemble guidance, and the feedback riddled GFS finally 
joining the offshore solutions, even small longitudinal adjustments 
in cyclone track would result in changes in the location of the 
deformation, stratiform rain band, and its wrn edge, so forecast 
confidence in impacts/rain over cntl NC remains only average. The 
most likely track would be far enough west to spread meaningful rain 
through much of the ern half of NC during the latter half of the 
weekend, with a sharp gradient between US-1 and I-95, and minimal 
amounts over the srn/wrn Piedmont. 

The aforementioned amplification of the nrn stream across the CONUS 
Thanksgiving week, in a progressive and energetic pattern with some 
stream phasing possible, should support another episode of coastal 
cyclogenesis near the South and Middle Atlantic coasts next Wed-Thu. 
That system has more potential to produce meaningful rain throughout 
the entirety of cntl NC, as the proximity of the nrn stream and 
forcing for ascent are forecast to be stronger and more favorably 
centered just inland, versus offshore in the case of this weekend's 
system. 

There are indications of yet another coastal low in this developing, 
energetic pattern next weekend (~28-29th Nov). Cntl NC will need far 
more hits than misses from each of these systems and those that 
follow, in order to alleviate the otherwise worsening drought and to 
verify the long advertised and awaited seasonal outlook for above 
average precipitation.
